I am 62 years old and I have farmed this land since I was a young woman. My husband taught me, and his mother taught him. In Quzhou, we grow winter wheat and summer maize — that is what this land is for, that is what the village does, that is what I know. My plot is about 8 mu total. The soil here is flat and good, but water is always a worry. I have to pump from deep underground.

I will plant wheat in October on all 7 mu of my main field, the same as every year. I buy seeds from the supply cooperative in town — last year I used Jimai 22, it did well, I will use it again. For fertilizer I do what I have always done: put down the base fertilizer before sowing, then add urea at jointing stage. My neighbor Mr. Zhang uses similar amounts and his wheat is fine. I irrigate three times — once before sowing to wet the seedbed, once at jointing, once at heading. If I skip heading irrigation the grain is light.

After wheat harvest in June I will plant maize immediately on the same 7 mu. I do not plow — no time, the maize needs to go in fast before the heat passes. I buy Xianyu 335 hybrid seed, everyone here uses it. Maize needs less irrigation than wheat, two times is enough if the summer rains come.

I also keep about 1 mu near the house for vegetables — garlic, cabbage, some tomatoes. Those are for eating and selling a little at market. I use old saved seeds for most of them.

I am getting older. I hire a machine for rotary tilling before wheat and for the wheat harvest. I do the rest myself or with my daughter-in-law when she visits.
